title: Screening answers: 8 logistics cases and 8 grounding cases
passRule: Logistics cases: the deterministic checks from evals/screening-logistics. Grounding cases: format, word band, dash and banned-word checks, then no fabricated claim by the Opus judge.
decisionRule:
Per site, pick the lowest-effort Haiku arm (order: low-nothink, low, medium, high) that satisfies ALL of:
1. Primary metric: its case failures are at most one more than the best Haiku arm (counting every case of every run). The 95% Wilson intervals are reported but do not qualify an arm (tightened before any paid run, 2026-10-22: at these sample sizes overlapping intervals admit several extra failures).
2. Hard constraints: for every hard-constraint metric it has no more violations than the gpt-oss arm, and zero violations for the metrics a site lists as absolute (ranking: hard-constraint violations in the top 10 must be 0; every site: no call over the 100k input budget).
3. It produced no errors (a thrown error, an empty reply, a budget stop) that the best Haiku arm did not also produce.
Tie-break between arms of the same effort rank: lower p50 per-call latency. If no arm qualifies the site is undecided and the orchestrator decides by hand.
gpt-oss is a baseline only: it is never a candidate. A winner with more primary failures than gpt-oss is flagged for the orchestrator. Cache hit rate and cost are reported but do not enter the rule.

**Q: Beschreiben Sie eine Situation, in der Sie einen Konflikt im Team gelöst haben.**

Im Jahr 2022 trat in einem meiner vier Softwareprojekte bei Nordlicht Software ein Konflikt zwischen zwei Entwicklern über die Architektur eines Schnittstellenmoduls auf. Ich organisierte ein moderiertes Gespräch, hörte beide Seiten an, fasste die technischen Argumente zusammen und erarbeitete gemeinsam ein einheitliches Vorgehen; anschließend verankerte ich das vereinbarte Design im Sprint‑Backlog und etablierte wöchentliche Fortschritts‑Checks. Der Konflikt war innerhalb einer Woche gelöst, das Modul wurde planmäßig fertiggestellt, die Projektverzögerung blieb bei null Prozent und die Kundenzufriedenheit stieg durch die termingerechte Lieferung.
---ANSWER_END---

**Q: How would you handle a prospect who goes silent after a demo?**

I would first review the prospect’s activity in Salesforce to see what content they engaged with and note any open questions. Next, I would send a concise follow‑up email that recaps the demo’s key ROI points, attaches a tailored summary, and proposes a short call to address any concerns. If there is still no response, I would reach out to another stakeholder identified during the demo, similar to how I re‑engaged a regional carrier that stopped using our dashboard; I rebuilt the onboarding with their operations lead, which led to a two‑year renewal. These steps keep momentum and demonstrate continued value.
---ANSWER_END---
